concepts.title: Yoga: Harmony of Body and Mind
concepts.definition: Yoga is an ancient Indian wisdom and cultural heritage focusing on harmony -- between body and mind, thought and action, restraint and fulfilment, human and nature. It is at once an art and a science of healthy living, aiming at a holistic approach to health and well-being.
concepts.key_idea: Yoga tunes the whole instrument -- body, breath, mind and world brought into one harmony.
concepts.textbook_ref: keks109.txt opening (ancient indian wisdom, cultural and spiritual heritage, harmony body mind, art and science of healthy living)
question_patterns: what is meant by yoga as harmony between body and mind

solution_steps.explain: Yoga's work is joining -- bringing into harmony the divisions within and around us.
Disciplined practice of posture, breath and attention cultivates that harmony.
Health and well-being follow as wholeness -- the art and science of living well.

concepts.title: The Eight Limbs: Ashtanga of Yoga
concepts.definition: Classical yoga is systematised as ashtanga -- eight limbs: yama and niyama of ethical living, asana for steady posture, pranayama for regulated breath, pratyahara withdrawing the senses, then dharana, dhyana and samadhi as progressive states of concentration and absorption.
concepts.key_idea: Eight limbs from ethics to absorption -- posture and breath are just the first rungs of a long ladder.
concepts.textbook_ref: keks109.txt limbs sections (ashtanga yoga, yama niyama asana pranayama pratyahara dharana dhyana samadhi)
question_patterns: name the eight limbs of yoga
in class 11 yoga chapter: what do yama and niyama cover
why is pranayama important in yoga practice
what is pratyahara and why does it precede concentration
explain how the eight limbs form a progressive path

solution_steps.explain: Yama and niyama lay the ethical base -- restraint and observance that steady life itself.
Asana stabilises the body; pranayama regulates the breath that links body and mind.
Pratyahara withdraws the senses; dharana holds attention; dhyana deepens into flow; samadhi completes the absorption.

concepts.title: Benefits of Yoga for Health and Well-being
concepts.definition: Regular yoga practice yields measurable benefits: flexibility and strength from asanas, calmer respiration and stress relief from pranayama, better concentration and emotional balance from meditative limbs. As preventive health, yoga addresses lifestyle disorders by working on the whole person rather than isolated symptoms.
concepts.key_idea: Practice pays in body and mind alike -- strength, calm, focus and resilience against lifestyle disease.
concepts.textbook_ref: keks109.txt benefits sections (flexibility, stress relief, concentration, lifestyle disorders, preventive health, well being)
question_patterns: what are the physical benefits of yoga practice
in class 11 yoga chapter: how does yoga help in stress management

what mental benefits follow from meditation and dhyana
design a simple daily yoga routine for a student

solution_steps.explain: Asanas improve flexibility, posture and strength while massaging internal systems.
Pranayama steadies respiration and emotion; meditative practice builds concentration and calm.
Practised regularly, yoga counters sedentary lifestyle disorders and sustains overall well-being.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A student thinks yoga means only asanas. Correct the picture using the eight limbs.

solution_template.explain: Asanas are indeed one limb -- the third -- and the most photographed.
Ethics (yama-niyama) come first, and breath regulation (pranayama) follows asanas.
Sense-withdrawal, concentration, meditation and samadhi complete the path beyond any gym routine.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A student facing exam stress begins ten minutes of daily pranayama and dhyana. Explain what changes the chapter would predict.

solution_template.explain: Slow, regulated breathing calms the nervous system, easing anxiety.
Daily dhyana strengthens concentration, improving study quality.
Together they illustrate yoga's preventive, whole-person approach to a modern problem.
